newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Shekel drops sharply against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Shekel drops sharply against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel representative rate was fixed sharply lower against the dollar on Monday as the American currency strengthened worldwide, dealers said.
"The shekel declined after the dollar rose on Friday against the mark and the yen," said Guy Levi of Bank Leumi.
"Trading was active but the rise of dollar had only minimal impact on the basket, which rose to 6.95 percent below the diagonal rate" he said.

The shekel is allowed to fluctuate in a trading band of seven percent above or below a sloping mid-point designed to devalue the Israeli currency at a rate of six percent a year against the basket of key currencies.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2620 shekels against 3.2490 shekels on Friday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6192 shekels against 3.6159 on Friday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.8032 shekels per 100 yen against 2.8136 on Friday and against the mark at 2.0542 shekels against 2.0591 on Friday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.2620 shekels.
